title: Desired-State Runtime: Environment-Scoped Compose and Docker Engine Apply
description: Move Bahia from environment-level, monolithic Compose operations toward Nostr-native structured service desired state that can render to Compose and Docker Engine targets first, while keeping Kubernetes and Podman as later renderer/adapter targets. This feature introduces typed desired-state domain models, environment-scoped apply locking, full-project Compose synthesis, Docker Engine desired-state apply, observation normalization and drift detection, legacy environment hydration, and additive Nostr/ContextVM status/result/read-model enrichment -- all without adding new Nostr event kinds or d-tag coordinates or breaking existing control-plane semantics.
dependencies: Existing ContextVM mutation flow (25910), canonical status/state/audit observables (30315/30900/30078/4903), and migration-only historical request/status/result/read-model fixtures where needed
Existing runtime resolver, factory, and adapter infrastructure
Docker Compose CLI (docker compose config, up, pull)
Docker Engine API for direct container operations
PostgreSQL advisory locking for environment-level serialization

actors.name: runtime_lifecycle_service
actors.role: Owns desired-state apply for Compose/Docker deploys, orchestrates build/render/apply/observe, holds environment advisory locks, and publishes correlated Nostr status/result events

actors.name: desired_state_builder
actors.role: Maps service/environment/artifact/runtime config/secrets into canonical desired service specs with Bahia labels and secret redaction

actors.name: environment_plan_assembler
actors.role: Loads active sibling services, hydrates missing snapshots from persisted state, computes environment revision hashes, and produces the full environment runtime plan

actors.name: compose_renderer
actors.role: Renders full-project Compose YAML, env files, and render metadata from the environment plan; validates with docker compose config; executes atomic swap and apply

actors.name: docker_renderer
actors.role: Maps desired service specs to Docker Engine container/host/network config; performs desired-hash comparison for no-op apply; manages container lifecycle

actors.name: observation_normalizer
actors.role: Normalizes Compose and Docker runtime observations into a comparable subset for drift detection

actors.name: nostr_projector
actors.role: Enriches existing ContextVM response and canonical status/read-model projections with desired-state metadata additively

in_scope: Typed desired-state domain model with JSONB persistence and hash columns
Canonical hash serialization with deterministic JSON, sorted keys, stable ordering, and golden fixtures
Environment-scoped DB advisory locking for Compose/Docker apply serialization
RuntimeLifecycleService refactor to shared internal deploy helper
Desired-state builder with Bahia label injection and secret ref separation
Legacy environment-plan hydration from persisted registry/runtime/artifact state
Compose phase 1: full-project synthesis to Bahia-owned compose_dir
Docker Engine phase 1: desired-state apply with hash-based no-op detection
Podman reuse of Docker-compatible desired-state path where feasible
Observation normalization for Compose and Docker into comparable subset
Drift detection: in_sync / drifted / unknown based on desired vs observed hash
Additive Nostr status step progression (building_desired_state, locking_environment, rendering, applying, observing, projecting)
Additive ContextVM response and read-model payload enrichment without new kinds or d-tag coordinates
Compose ownership gate for Bahia-owned compose_dir validation
Renderer-specific typed extension payloads (Compose, Docker) stored as JSONB
out_of_scope: Compose phase 2 per-service fragment optimization (deferred until full-project synthesis is stable)
Kubernetes desired-state implementation (stays on legacy deploy path)
Podman-specific desired-state design beyond Docker-compatible reuse
New Nostr event kinds or d-tag coordinate changes
Platform rewrite of reactor, authorization, event validation, or endpoint aliasing

terminal_semantics.principle: Desired-state apply completion is determined by explicit terminal signals, never by polling or timeout-based heuristics
details: Deploy execution completes when the runtime adapter returns a terminal apply result (success or failure), not after elapsed time
Advisory locks are released deterministically via defer, not via timeout expiry
Nostr status events report explicit step progression; terminal results are published as correlated ContextVM responses and canonical observables with explicit success/failure payloads
Observation is attempted synchronously after apply; failure paths persist explicit failure state rather than leaving unknown state
Drift detection compares deterministic hashes, not polling-derived snapshots
No ticker-based reconciliation or periodic polling is part of the approved desired-state contract

risks.title: Compose directory ownership
risks.description: Accidentally treating a non-Bahia-owned compose_dir as managed could destroy operator-authored Compose files
risks.mitigation: Gate phase 1 behind validation that the target directory is dedicated to Bahia-managed services

risks.title: Legacy environment hydration
risks.description: First render must include sibling services that lack desired snapshots; missing hydration would remove services from generated output
risks.mitigation: Reconstruct missing sibling specs from current persisted registry/runtime/artifact state and persist opportunistically

risks.title: Rollback safety
risks.description: Additive DB columns and Nostr fields are safe for old readers, but older application code must be validated against generated Compose projects

risks.title: Concurrency tradeoff
risks.description: Environment-level advisory locking reduces Docker parallelism compared to service-level locking
risks.mitigation: Accept tradeoff for consistent behavior across runtimes

risks.title: Secret exposure in generated files
risks.description: Generated Compose env files may contain resolved secrets
risks.mitigation: Test ownership, permissions, cleanup, and redaction of generated env files

risks.title: Renderer observation drift
risks.description: Compose and Docker must normalize observations into the same semantic subset to avoid false drift
risks.mitigation: Shared normalization contract with golden test fixtures for parity

open_questions: Does 5961 deploy currently reach RuntimeLifecycleService directly, or through an intermediate orchestration layer that must be refactored before the shared deploy helper lands?

Operators must decide which staging/production compose_dir targets are Bahia-owned before rollout; bahia_owned records that decision per runtime target and defaults checked-in staging/production targets to blocked unless markers prove ownership.
